newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile confident copper prices will stay high.
newsitem.headline: Chile confident copper prices will stay high.

text.p: Copper prices, which have surged in the last two weeks, are likely to remain at current levels for a while as the result of lower inventories and rising demand, said Chile's state copper studies center Cochilco.
"We tend to think that current (price) levels could be maintained for a more prolonged period," Aldo Picozzi, market studies manager at Cochilco, told Reuters.
Copper prices jumped four cents Thursday on London Metal Exchange to $1.17 a lb.

The rally is the result of a combination of a fall in inventories, a drop in scrap metal sales and strong demand from the United States, south-east Asia and Europe, with the exception of Germany, said Picozzi.
"The market is presenting very positive signs and the price is reflecting market conditions," he said.
Although scrap sales could rise in coming weeks, Cochilco does not expect prices to fall -- at least in the short term, said Picozzi.
